clue.text: Require last of wine in study to be brought over

indicators.note: bringing something over flips it, so the letters run the other way
one item placed in another is enclosed by it

parts.note: a den is a private study room

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter

parts.note: 'last of' keeps the final letter

explanation.surface: Someone needs the dregs of their wine fetched to the study.
explanation.walkthrough: The wine's last letter goes inside DEN to make DEEN, and then the whole thing is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To need something is to require it; the two verbs are plain synonyms.

clue.text: Now for the first time, left IOW town

parts.note: something new is happening now for the first time
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: Someone has just now left a town on the Isle of Wight.
explanation.walkthrough: IOW is the Isle of Wight, an island off England's south coast; port is the nautical word for left.
explanation.definitionFit: Newport is the county town of the Isle of Wight.

clue.text: Painter from southern state

indicators.note: letters taken from the words that follow are lifted out of them

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: An artist comes from a southern state.
explanation.definitionFit: Max Ernst was a German-born Surrealist and Dada painter.

clue.text: Run away from stalker on cycle

parts.note: a turn is one cycle or rotation
someone who tails a person follows them secretly

explanation.surface: Someone flees on a bicycle from a person stalking them.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' places the stalker piece after the cycle piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn tail is an idiom for fleeing, as an animal shows its tail when it bolts.

clue.text: Finest fruit for most important person

parts.note: the top one is the finest
a banana is a fruit

explanation.surface: The best fruit is reserved for the VIP.
explanation.definitionFit: Top banana is informal slang, from American vaudeville, for the leader or boss.

clue.text: Come back with extremely rare dog

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its outermost letters

parts.note: first and last letters
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: Someone returns with a very unusual dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely rare' looks like 'very rare' but asks for the word's ends.
explanation.definitionFit: To recur is to happen again, to come back after an interval.

clue.text: A reserve tutor somehow makes a valuable discovery

indicators.note: somehow says the letters are rearranged in some unspecified way

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A stand-in teacher stumbles on something precious.
explanation.definitionFit: Treasure trove is buried treasure found by chance, hence any valuable find.

clue.text: Put in, batting, played for time

parts.note: a cricketer batting is in
to stall is to delay in order to gain time

explanation.surface: A batsman who came in deliberately slowed the game.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the side batting is 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Equipment that has been installed has been put in place and fitted.

clue.text: Old shoes for those collecting shellfish?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: pointed-toed shoes fashionable in the 1950s and 60s
second meaning, read literally: people who gather small sea snails

explanation.walkthrough: A winkle is a small edible sea snail, so its gatherers are literally winkle pickers; the shoes were named for their sharp points, like the pin used to eat winkles.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is a set term for the long-pointed shoes and also a literal description of gatherers of periwinkles.

clue.text: Terribly relevant, read about women's perfume

indicators.note: letters placed about something surround it
done terribly means done badly, out of proper order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
W is the abbreviation for women's

explanation.surface: Someone reads up, most pertinently, on women's scent.
explanation.definitionFit: Lavender water is a light fragrance distilled from lavender flowers, a classic scent.

clue.text: Wager over a Greek character

parts.note: a bet is a wager
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bet is placed on someone from Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' places the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Beta is the second letter of the Greek alphabet, and a letter is a character.

clue.text: Antony's wife in new coat, by the way

indicators.note: something made new is refashioned, so these letters take a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written
via means by way of

explanation.surface: Antony's wife, in a new coat, mentioned as an aside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By the way' looks like a throwaway aside but supplies the Latin-derived word for 'by way of'.
explanation.definitionFit: Octavia, sister of Octavian, was Mark Antony's wife, as in Shakespeare's Antony and Cleopatra.

clue.text: Excessively optimistic, girl at conclusion of programme

parts.note: Rose is a girl's name
taken as written

indicators.note: the conclusion of a word is its final letter

parts.note: last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A girl is overly hopeful at the end of a TV show.
explanation.definitionFit: Rose-tinted, rosy views are unrealistically hopeful, a figurative sense of the colour word.

clue.text: Teach painting back home

indicators.note: going back means reading from the end to the start

parts.note: painting is a form of art
being in means being at home

explanation.surface: Someone returns home to teach painting.
explanation.definitionFit: To train someone is to instruct or coach them in a skill.

clue.text: A second page on pheasant eating a vegetable

indicators.note: something eating another takes it inside
in a down clue, one piece on another sits above it, so the opening letters come before the bird

parts.note: taken as written
S is the abbreviation for second
P is the abbreviation for page
the argus is a large Asian pheasant
taken as written

explanation.surface: On page two, a pheasant is shown eating vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: The argus pheasant, with eyespots on its feathers, is named after the many-eyed giant of Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Asparagus is a vegetable whose young shoots are eaten.

clue.text: A pound in one country or another

indicators.note: placed in something means enclosed by it

parts.note: Austria is a European country
L, from Latin libra, is the pound sign
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pound coin is spent in some country or other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One country or another' reads as a vague phrase; split it, the first country is the container and 'another' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Australia is a different nation from Austria, so it is 'another' country beside the first one.

clue.text: It speaks for itself, one mayor's in difficulty

indicators.note: letters in difficulty are in disorder, knocked out of place

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A mayor in trouble says the situation is self-evident.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is used to signal that something is understood without further explanation, as a thing that is obvious.

clue.text: County type pair confused crossing river

indicators.note: letters crossing something straddle it, sitting on either side
confused letters are jumbled out of their order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A muddled couple cross a river somewhere in the county.
explanation.definitionFit: Tipperary is a county in Ireland, famous from the wartime song.

clue.text: Characters in class

definitions.meaning: first meaning: printed letters, as in typeface
second meaning: a category or kind

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like people in a classroom; the two words are separate senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both printing characters collectively and a sort or class of thing.

clue.text: Organised tour round duke' house

indicators.note: going round something encloses it
organised letters are rearranged into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
D is the abbreviation for duke

explanation.surface: A guided tour takes visitors round a duke's stately home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House' here means a royal dynasty, not a building, despite the stately-home tour.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tudors were the English royal dynasty from Henry VII to Elizabeth I, a royal house.

clue.text: Deep regret about son breaking in again

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: breaking in means forcing a way inside

parts.note: more, as in 'once more', means again
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A parent deeply regrets their son burgling again.
explanation.definitionFit: Remorse is the guilt-laden sorrow felt over a wrong one has done.

clue.text: Doctor receiving one cable about a peruke

indicators.note: turned about means facing the other way
something receiving others takes them inside itself

parts.note: a GP is a general practitioner
I is the Roman numeral for one
a cable is a wire

explanation.surface: A doctor gets a telegram about a wig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like 'concerning' but turns the whole assembled string round; GP is the British term for a family doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A peruke and a periwig are both old words for the long wig worn in the 17th and 18th centuries.

clue.text: Agree fare

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to be on friendly terms
second meaning: to do or manage, as in 'how are you getting on?'

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fare' looks like a ticket price but is the verb meaning to get along.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to have a good relationship with someone and to progress or manage.

clue.text: Type of marsupial — very large number seen across Italian river

indicators.note: letters seen across something stretch from one side of it to the other

parts.note: OS stands for outsize
the Po is Italy's longest river
a sum is a number arrived at by adding

explanation.surface: A vast number of marsupials have been spotted across an Italian river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very large number' reads as one phrase but splits: 'very large' gives one piece and 'number' another.
explanation.definitionFit: The opossum is a North and South American pouched mammal, so it is one kind of marsupial.

clue.text: Form of address used in India has upset one bishop

definitions.text: Form of address used in India

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so read from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A colonial-era form of address has annoyed a bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: Sahib was the respectful term used in India for a man, especially a European, meaning master or sir.

clue.text: Achieve one's full potential using it in meeting

indicators.note: placed in something means set inside it

parts.note: a get-together is an informal meeting
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone reaches their best by putting IT to work in meetings.
explanation.walkthrough: The small word goes between the first word of the meeting phrase and the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To get it together is an informal idiom for getting organised and fulfilling one's abilities.

clue.text: Alienate corrupt sergeant

indicators.note: corrupted letters are spoiled from their proper order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A crooked sergeant drives others away.
explanation.definitionFit: To estrange people is to make them unfriendly or distant, a close synonym of alienate.

clue.text: Initially one blows on each instrument

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each following word

parts.note: first letters of the four words

explanation.surface: At the start, a player blows on every wind instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The oboe is a double-reed woodwind instrument, and indeed one that is blown.
